subject: horticulture
intro: Horticulture leads to careers across the plant industries: growing and propagating in nurseries and greenhouses, maintaining landscapes, protecting plants from pests, and researching soils and crop science.

roles.title: Soil and Plant Scientists
roles.what: Research the breeding, physiology, production and management of crops, trees, shrubs and nursery stock, study how soil composition affects plant growth, and investigate how alternative practices change productivity and pest control.
roles.where: Plant nutrition and the root environment — photosynthesis, soil types and texture, water and nutrient management — plus the pests and diseases unit are exactly the science this research career deepens.

roles.title: Landscaping and Groundskeeping Workers
roles.what: Landscape and maintain grounds using hand and power tools: mow, trim and dig, lay sod, plant and water, fertilise, and install sprinklers to keep parks, gardens and properties in good condition.
roles.where: Plant classification and structure helps you choose and site plants correctly, while the aftercare of young plants and water and nutrient management topics are the daily maintenance this work performs.

roles.title: Farmworkers and Laborers, Crop, Nursery, and Greenhouse
roles.what: Manually plant, cultivate and harvest vegetables, fruits, nuts and horticultural specialties: till soil, transplant and prune, apply fertilisers and pesticides, and clean, grade and pack what the crop yields.
roles.where: The propagation unit — seed, cuttings and grafting — and growing media and glasshouse practice from the horticultural practice unit are the nursery and greenhouse production skills this job uses.

roles.title: Pest Control Workers
roles.what: Inspect premises for pests, identify infestations and damage, and apply integrated and chemical control measures safely, following state licensing rules to keep buildings and landscapes free of harmful organisms.
roles.where: The pests, diseases and disorders unit — pest life cycles, disease diagnosis, integrated and chemical control — plus pesticide safety awareness are the foundation of licensed pest management work.
